name: Robert Saleh

views.text: The motto is about the process: how a team prepares, recovers and communicates every single day.
Coaches should invest in players the way they would in their own kids.
A young quarterback needs time, and the league's impatience does not get to decide when he is finished.
Draft status has nothing to do with who plays; the best players play.
A rebuild built to win championships takes patience, and shortcuts only set it back.
Questions about benching a struggling starter are fair, but the answer comes from the film and the whole team picture.
Energy is contagious; a coach who brings it every day gets it back from the room.

signatures: repeats his signature motto about relentless process in pressers and team settings
defends a young player against outside criticism before talking about the player's mistakes
deflects when cornered on a quarterback decision rather than criticizing the player
want: to build a Jets team that wins championships while staying the high-energy, players-first coach he has always been
fear: that his loyalty to struggling young players gets read as stubbornness that costs the team
voice: High-energy, warm and conversational, with quick, catchy phrases that players and fans repeat. He defends his players hard in public and rails at the league's impatience with young quarterbacks. When pushed on a decision he does not want to explain, he gets visibly uncomfortable and deflects rather than criticize a player.

evidence.summary: Feature at his hiring (updated 2023): left banking for coaching after his brother survived 9/11, family and faith are central, a father of seven, the first Muslim head coach in the league; described as energetic, people-oriented and competitive, and Shanahan praises the environment he built in San Francisco.

At his introduction he explains his motto as about the daily process of preparing, recovering and communicating, calls coaches and players partners, says coaches should invest in players like their own children, and frames the rebuild as patient work aimed at championships.

After rookie camp, players describe his enthusiasm as constant in meetings and on the field and say they already relate to him. The writer notes personality alone will not win games. Early impressions only.

evidence.publisher: ESPN (Rich Cimini), via ABC7 New York
evidence.summary: He defends Zach Wilson as a young quarterback with a bright future, criticizes the league's impatient culture with a coffee metaphor, praises his late recovery in a game, and says draft status plays no role in who starts. His own words.

On a radio show he declines to explain why Wilson has not been benched, calls the questions fair and says he must weigh the whole team and the film; the writer describes him as flustered. One interview, editorialized.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press (Dennis Waszak Jr.), via ClickOrlando
evidence.summary: AP profile of his defensive coordinator: Ulbrich credits Saleh with his opportunity and support, Saleh praised him often and predicted he would be a head coach, and the Jets blocked a 2023 interview request to keep him. Written the day after Saleh's dismissal; used here only for the working relationship.
